# Topic A — Odds, Log-odds & the Logistic Model


## Q1 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Convert between the three scales for p = 0.2.

```{r q1-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
p <- 0.2
odds <- p / (1 - p)
logit <- log(odds)
round(c(p = p, odds = odds, logit = logit), 4)
# back again
round(c(odds = exp(logit), p = exp(logit) / (1 + exp(logit)), plogis = plogis(logit)), 4)
```

# Topic B — Interpreting Coefficients


## Q6 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Model low ~ lwt (mother's weight in pounds).

```{r q6-data, eval=TRUE}
library(MASS)        # birthwt data
bw <- birthwt
bw$smoke_f <- factor(bw$smoke, labels = c("no", "yes"))
bw$race_f <- factor(bw$race, labels = c("white", "black", "other"))
```

```{r q6-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
m2 <- glm(low ~ lwt, family = binomial, data = bw)
round(coef(m2), 4)
round(exp(coef(m2)["lwt"]), 4)          # odds ratio per extra pound
round(exp(10 * coef(m2)["lwt"]), 4)     # per extra 10 pounds
```

# Topic C — Evaluating Models: Deviance, AIC, z


## Q11 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Compare the null and residual deviance of m3 and read the AIC.

```{r q11-data, eval=TRUE}
library(MASS)        # birthwt data
bw <- birthwt
bw$smoke_f <- factor(bw$smoke, labels = c("no", "yes"))
bw$race_f <- factor(bw$race, labels = c("white", "black", "other"))
```

```{r q11-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
m3 <- glm(low ~ smoke_f + lwt, family = binomial, data = bw)
round(c(null_dev = m3$null.deviance, resid_dev = m3$deviance, AIC = AIC(m3)), 3)
# AIC = deviance + 2 * (number of coefficients)
round(m3$deviance + 2 * length(coef(m3)), 3)
```

# Topic D — Prediction & Classification


## Q16 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Turn predicted probabilities from the best model into 0/1 predictions and make a confusion matrix.

```{r q16-data, eval=TRUE}
library(MASS)        # birthwt data
bw <- birthwt
bw$smoke_f <- factor(bw$smoke, labels = c("no", "yes"))
bw$race_f <- factor(bw$race, labels = c("white", "black", "other"))
```

```{r q16-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
# the model chosen by step() in Q14 (written out so this chunk runs on its own)
best <- glm(low ~ smoke_f + lwt + race_f + ptl + ht + ui, family = binomial, data = bw)
p_hat <- predict(best, type = "response")
pred <- ifelse(p_hat >= 0.5, 1, 0)
cm <- table(actual = bw$low, predicted = pred)
cm
accuracy <- mean(pred == bw$low)
round(accuracy, 4)
```

## Q20 · L5 · Scenario 2

**Goal:** Simulate 1,000 loan applicants (`set.seed(20)`) whose default probability depends on income and debt ratio, fit a logistic model, interpret the odds ratios, and choose a threshold that keeps the false-positive rate below 20%. Write a 4-sentence report for a loan officer.

```{r q20-data, eval=TRUE}
set.seed(20)
n <- 1000
income <- round(rlnorm(n, log(50), 0.4), 1)           # $1000s
debt_ratio <- round(runif(n, 0, 0.8), 2)
p_default <- plogis(-1 - 0.03 * income + 4 * debt_ratio)
loans <- data.frame(income, debt_ratio, default = rbinom(n, 1, p_default))
```

```{r q20-l5}
# 1. glm(default ~ income + debt_ratio, family = binomial)
# 2. Odds ratios: per $10,000 income and per +0.1 debt ratio
# 3. False-positive rate (good customers flagged) for thresholds 0.2-0.6
# 4. The lowest threshold with FPR < 0.20
# 5. Report (4 sentences as comments):
```
